papers.title: Cross-subject EEG driving fatigue detection: early personal spectral reference and causal long-sequence residual encoding.
papers.summary: Proposes a cross-subject EEG driving-fatigue decoder that uses an early personal spectral reference from a short session-opening window and causal long-sequence residual encoding. It reports leave-one-subject-out macro-F1 of 0.655 ± 0.005 on MPD-DF and RMSE of 0.209/0.200 on SEED-VIG, outperforming matched absolute-spectrum baselines under shared parameters.

papers.title: From features to digital biomarkers: EEG-fNIRS classification pipelines for brain monitoring.
papers.summary: Reviews EEG- and fNIRS-based machine learning classification pipelines for brain monitoring, organizing them by target formulation, preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Across 117 primary studies, most reported measures remained candidate biomarkers, only four reached qualified independent clinical validation, and none evaluated clinical utility.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.summary: The paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network using modal re-weighting and a bidirectional Mamba encoder to learn contextual information across epochs. On Sleep-EDF and ISRUC datasets, MM-SleepNet outperformed state-of-the-art methods, and ablation experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of its modules.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.summary: The study evaluated a multi-domain EEG decoding framework for self-imagined emotion recognition using time-frequency features, functional and effective connectivity, and subject-specific calibration in 38 participants. PLV-based features with SVM achieved 97.0% accuracy under pooled cross-validation but only ~25–30% under leave-one-subject-out, while subject-specific calibration using 75% of target data restored accuracy to 95.0%.

papers.title: Revisiting EEG slowing in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder: rhythms, background, and phenoconversion.
papers.summary: This paper revisits EEG slowing in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, examining rhythms, background activity, and phenoconversion; no abstract was supplied, so specific findings cannot be stated.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.summary: Using whole-night EEG and fNIRS in healthy young adults, the study characterized cortical hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states, showing slow-frequency (0.002–0.1 Hz) power increased in N1 and attenuated across N2/N3, while very-low-frequency (<0.01 Hz) power re-emerged in REM. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15–0.5 Hz) were enhanced during NREM sleep and returned toward wake-like levels in REM.

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.summary: The paper introduces KimiFormer, a lightweight hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw wearable EEG for affective state recognition, using a spatio-temporal stemming module and stacked Conformer blocks with linear/full attention. It achieved 95.5% accuracy on the EEG Violence Dataset but near-chance subject-independent performance on DREAMER (balanced accuracy 52.7% valence, 50.2% arousal), with 3.2M parameters and 15.64 ms inference latency.

papers.title: Spreading depolarization, not seizure activity, drives immediate early gene expression in mouse cortex after electroconvulsive stimulation
papers.summary: Recorded cortical responses to electroconvulsive stimulation in mouse dorsal cortex and found that spreading depolarization, rather than seizure activity, accounted for increased Fos expression and was associated with EEG features predicting positive ECT outcomes in patients. The results implicate SD as a possible mediator of ECT's plasticity effects and biomarker.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.summary: Compared Hjorth parameters, fractal-dimension measures, and conventional spectral band-power features for EEG-based stress detection using ANOVA-based feature selection and multiple machine-learning classifiers on pre-recorded stress-experiment data. Hjorth activity, frontal β asymmetry, and the γ/θ ratio were among the most frequently selected features, and combined feature spaces including Hjorth parameters and fractal dimensions outperformed the conventional spectral-feature reference configuration.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of a balanced two-night crossover in 72 healthy adults assessing how ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) and first-night effect alter polysomnographic sleep indices and EEG power. Both ABPM and first-night effect were associated with lower composite sleep quality index, ABPM with higher light-sleep and lower N3 percentages and higher relative theta power, and 60.3% of in-sleep ABPM measurements contained at least one arousal detection within the 2-min window.

papers.title: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
papers.summary: Used EEG from 226 participants (advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls) with a 21-feature neurodynamic profiling approach and machine learning to identify shared and tradition-specific signatures. Meditation was reliably separable from task states via a large uniform drop in complexity, while meditators differed from controls mainly in timescale dynamics, and a classifier trained on three traditions detected meditation in the held-out fourth, relying mainly on complexity features.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG from 33 term neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and found significantly higher HFO rates in those with seizures (0.12 vs 0.03 HFOs/min/channel; AUC 0.81 at a 0.07 threshold). HFO rate was the strongest contributor in multivariable seizure-classification models combining EEG background and MRI findings.

papers.title: Reproducible EEG-BCI Experiments: Frame-Confirmed Timing and Physical SSVEP Validation.
papers.summary: Presented and evaluated an auditable EEG-BCI experimental workflow integrating machine-readable SSVEP protocols, deterministic session planning, frame-confirmed events, acquisition provenance, integrity checks, and photoresistor-based display validation. All 61 automated tests passed; 48 of 48 optical sweep measurements (8-15 Hz) fell within ±0.25 Hz (mean absolute error 0.0345 Hz, max 0.0668 Hz), though local optical pulse-width anomalies were observed at 13-14 Hz and in two multi-stimulus repetitions.

papers.title: Self-Organized Explainable Symbolic EEG Feature Engineering Using Directed Lobish and Previous-Next Pattern: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Dementia Classification.
papers.summary: Designed an interpretable symbolic EEG feature-engineering framework (SOXFE) combining Bipartite Channel Transformer, Previous-Next Pattern, cumulative-weight INCA selection, Directed Lobish explainability, and ensemble tkNN with combinational majority voting for dementia classification. Segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation reached 99.12-99.74% accuracy, but participant-independent accuracy fell to 51.19-63.81% (LOSO) and 49.00-62.50% (nested participant-grouped), with no McNemar advantage over majority-class baselines, so clinical diagnostic utility was not established.

papers.title: BioTWavePat: An EEG-Based Mental Performance Detection Model.
papers.summary: Introduced BioTWavePat-XFE, an EEG mental performance detection model using signed cross-rhythm channel-rank transition features, cumulative-weighted selectors, and Directed Lobish decoding, evaluated under three data-dependent selection protocols with participant-wise LOSO validation. Under leakage-restricted Protocol C, accuracies fell to 80.46% (STEW), 82.50% (TMPD), and 74.65% (MAT), showing whole-dataset selection inflated original estimates, with MAT near majority-prediction performance.

papers.title: Altered directional brain-heart interactions across resting states and frequency bands in schizophrenia.
papers.summary: Recorded simultaneous resting-state EEG and ECG in 33 medicated men with schizophrenia and 29 healthy men during eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions to assess directional brain-heart interaction across frequency bands. Patients showed reduced global-average brain-to-heart high-frequency coupling across all five EEG bands during eyes-open rest, alongside elevated theta, alpha, and beta EEG power, indicating altered statistical brain-heart coupling in schizophrenia.

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.summary: Presents a perspective arguing that low-friction, high-adherence passive sleep-tracking devices such as smart rings, despite lower accuracy than EEG/PSG gold standards, may be preferable for longitudinal monitoring of neurodegenerative disease. Argues that long-term statistical benefits from detecting within-person changes and higher sampling frequency can offset accuracy trade-offs, with focus on Parkinson's disease sleep monitoring.

papers.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model (CNN-GRU) with MRMR for EEG-Based Depression Detection.
papers.summary: Proposed a hybrid CNN-GRU deep learning framework with mRMR feature selection for EEG-based depression detection, evaluated on the MODMA dataset. Across 30 simulation runs, it achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.74%, outperforming the comparison methods.

papers.title: Explainable Rhythm-Resolved EEG for Retrospective Comparison of Psychiatric-Service Adults with Recorded Violent Offences and Non-Clinical Controls.
papers.summary: Applied rhythm-resolved rank-transition EEG features (RhythmFluxPat) with an explainable classifier to retrospectively separate psychiatric-service adults with recorded violent offences from non-clinical controls. A nested tkNN classified 93/95 participants (97.89%), with DRLobish linking features to delta and beta-to-gamma versus theta and alpha-to-theta rhythm routes, while the authors caution these are optimistic internal estimates.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations and Their Association with Cognitive Performance in Late-Onset Epilepsy of Unknown Etiology: Comparison with Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG microstate dynamics among 60 patients with late-onset epilepsy of unknown etiology (LOEU), 65 with Alzheimer's disease, and 60 cognitively normal controls, testing associations with MoCA and MMSE scores. LOEU and AD showed longer microstate B duration and lower microstate C occurrence than controls, LOEU had longer microstate D duration than both groups, and in LOEU longer microstate A duration was associated with lower cognitive scores.

papers.title: Sensor-Based Hand and Upper-Limb Movement Intention Recognition in Post-Stroke Rehabilitation: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-ScR scoping review mapping sensor-based hand and upper-limb movement intention recognition after stroke across 17 eligible studies, comprising EMG/myoelectric, EEG/BCI, EMG-triggered FES, and multimodal feedback systems. The review found development mainly through parallel EMG-based and EEG/BCI-based approaches, with true multimodal sensor fusion uncommon and no standardized framework.

papers.title: Reactive and predictive processes during unpredictable driving collisions in virtual reality: an exploratory immersive study with multimodal neurophysiological monitoring
papers.summary: Used a wearable dry-electrode EEG and photoplethysmography headset in virtual reality to test whether neural activity differentiates unpredictable collision from no-collision events in 16 participants across 120 trials. Post-stimulus clusters differentiated conditions with up to 93.8% cross-validated decoding accuracy, whereas pre-stimulus time-domain discrimination was at chance; a pre-stimulus broadband spectral difference survived correction but is exploratory and requires replication.

papers.title: Quantum-Kernel Learning for Subject-Independent EEG Emotion Recognition with Spectral-Connectivity Features.
papers.summary: Investigated state-fidelity-based quantum-kernel SVM learning for subject-independent EEG valence and arousal recognition using differential entropy and phase-locking value features from the DEAP dataset. Quantum-kernel SVM reached the highest mean balanced accuracy of 59.18% for valence, while Linear SVM with DE features led arousal at 54.16%, with comparable overall performance across classifiers.

papers.title: The perioperative sensory-cognitive interface: multimodal neuroimaging of hierarchical network reconfiguration in perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.summary: A review proposing a sensory-cognitive interface framework for perioperative neurocognitive disorders, synthesizing perioperative MRI and EEG evidence on thalamocortical routing, network integration, and recovery trajectories. The authors argue symptoms may depend on which hierarchical networks recover and when, and propose structural-functional connectivity coupling as one candidate measurement rather than an established biomarker.

papers.title: Interpersonal alignment in infra-slow EEG rhythms and bodily signals anticipates mutual recognition
papers.summary: Recorded infra-slow EEG alongside respiratory, cardiac and skin conductance signals during the perceptual crossing hyperscanning paradigm, contrasting dyads that achieved mutual recognition with those that did not. Mutual recognition trials showed enhanced inter-participant alignment of 0.1 Hz infra-slow EEG power and differences in respiratory depth, cardiac vagal index and skin conductance, suggesting infra-slow rhythms as a temporal scaffold for interpersonal brain-body coordination.

papers.title: Investigation of Brain Performance in the Schizophrenia Spectrum Using EEG with Mental and Temporal Effort.
authors: Bernadete Márcia Voichcoski Franco da Rosa
papers.summary: In 25 clinically stable schizophrenia patients and 11 healthy controls, EEG combined with a timed mental effort task showed that after effort, schizophrenia patients had 7.89% lower Vtotal and 16.35% lower frequency parameter, and only 6.1% of patients sustained full effort duration versus 57.9% of controls.

papers.title: Potter-Optimized Multiscale Bayesian Gated Axial Quantized Attention Network for Robust Multichannel EEG-ECG-Based Seizure Prediction.
papers.summary: Proposed a Potter-Optimized Multiscale Bayesian Gated Axial Quantized Attention Network (PM-BGAQAN) for three-state EEG-ECG seizure prediction, combining adaptive weighted mean filtering, a Convolutional Swin-Transformer, Bayesian asymmetric quantization, multiscale gated axial reverse attention, and Potter optimization. Evaluated on the Siena Scalp EEG and SeizeIT2 wearable datasets, it reported 99.86% overall classification accuracy and 98.06% subject-independent average accuracy.

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 49 acute ischemic stroke patients, a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) from a 7-min EEG within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with malignant cerebral edema (AUC 0.888 for lesion-ADR + ΔT) and functional outcomes, with associations attenuated for 90-day outcome after adjusting for admission NIHSS.

papers.title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
papers.summary: This PRISMA 2020 systematic review synthesized nine simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies (eight cohorts; N=377) in strictly defined adult major depressive disorder and found moderate-to-strong correlations between EEG-fMRI metrics and severity, notably for anhedonia (r=0.47 and 0.69), while evidence certainty remained low due to bias risk, imprecision, and analytical heterogeneity. The authors concluded that generalizable resting-state biomarkers are insufficient but that strong neurophysiological correlates emerge in active contexts such as neurofeedback and ketamine.

papers.title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Combined with General Anesthesia in Minimally Invasive Surgery for Lung Cancer: A Randomized, Patient- and Assessor-Blinded, Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In this randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, sham-controlled trial of 109 patients undergoing minimally invasive lung cancer surgery, perioperative transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation reduced postoperative VAS pain scores at 6 h (mean difference -1.900) and 24 h (-1.391) but not at 48 h, and lowered PCIA sufentanil consumption and pump presses. Exploratory EEG analysis found FDR-corrected power differences predominantly in beta-band oscillations across prefrontal, occipital, parietal, temporal, and diencephalic regions.

papers.title: Neurophysiological evidence for rapid semantic integration via fast mapping.
papers.summary: In an EEG study of 60 participants, novel item-label pairs encoded via fast mapping with high visual-semantic overlap produced an N400 semantic priming effect over a parietal electrode cluster, significantly larger than after low-overlap encoding, despite no significant behavioral priming. This provides neurophysiological evidence that high-overlap fast mapping enables rapid semantic integration within minutes of learning.

papers.title: Simultaneous EEG - fMRI study of brain activity during the autobiographical memory task in depressed patients with suicidal ideation.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous EEG-fMRI during an autobiographical memory test in 29 healthy controls, 25 depressed patients without suicidal ideation, and 20 depressed patients with suicidal ideation, this study found reduced specific autobiographical memories and slower memory construction in the suicidal ideation group, with lower left-hemisphere activation (SFGmed, calcarine, middle frontal gyrus) during construction; SFGmed activation remained specifically associated with suicidal ideation after controlling for depressive severity. EEG-informed fMRI further showed reduced left angular gyrus, superior frontal gyrus, SFGmed, and supplementary motor area activation in the suicidal ideation group during elaboration.

papers.title: Processed Electroencephalography-Guided Total Intravenous Anesthesia in a Malignant Hyperthermia-Susceptible Child Undergoing Ventricular Septal Defect Repair: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes the anesthetic management of a two-year-old, 10.4-kg child with a likely pathogenic RYR1 variant undergoing ventricular septal defect repair with cardiopulmonary bypass, using trigger-free propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia with SedLine processed EEG monitoring (raw EEG, SEF95, density spectral array). The intraoperative course was uneventful with no malignant hyperthermia features, illustrating the feasibility of pEEG-guided TIVA in this population and the value of spectral displays over single index values during hypothermia and rewarming.

papers.title: Patient-specific heart rate modulates developmental electrophysiology in transcriptomic-guided in silico models of pediatric human atrial cardiomyocytes.
papers.summary: Incorporated patient-specific intrinsic heart rates into transcriptomic-guided in silico populations of pediatric human atrial cardiomyocytes from 117 patients and simulated them at intrinsic and fixed pacing rates, with and without isoproterenol. Developmental electrophysiology differences persisted under fixed-rate pacing, and intrinsic-rate simulations showed stronger age associations for upstroke velocity and alternans, indicating both intrinsic developmental remodeling and rate-dependent modulation.

papers.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
authors: International League Against Epilepsy Acute Symptomatic Seizure Task Force
papers.summary: Conducted an international vignette-based survey of 963 respondents from 92 countries to characterize variation in acute symptomatic seizure management across etiologies. ASM initiation decisions showed high heterogeneity, with etiology the strongest driver but geography and provider characteristics also influencing ASM initiation, treatment duration, and cEEG use.

papers.title: The association between depressive symptoms, physical activity, flow state, and resting-state EEG in college students.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 216 college students, physical exercise was associated with fewer depressive symptoms and greater flow proneness, and frontal EEG lateralization differed by depressive symptoms, but EEG-related indirect effects in serial mediation models became non-significant after adjustment for sex and self-rated physical health, whereas the flow-related indirect effect remained significant.

papers.title: Propofol Target-Controlled Infusion with the Eleveld Model in Opioid-Sparing and Opioid-Free Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: Narratively reviewed how non-opioid adjuvants (dexmedetomidine, magnesium sulfate, ketamine, and lidocaine) may interact with Eleveld-model propofol target-controlled infusion dosing. Reported that dexmedetomidine reduces propofol requirements, magnesium reduces requirements to a lesser extent, ketamine's interaction is additive, and lidocaine's sparing effect is mainly context-dependent during stimulation.

papers.title: Interrupted-Sampling Repeater Jamming Suppression for Frequency-Agile Radar Based on Time-Frequency Analysis and Multi-Domain Filtering.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a joint time-frequency analysis and multi-domain filtering method to suppress interrupted-sampling repeater jamming in frequency-agile radar, using STFT-based two-dimensional feature extraction and adaptive notch filtering; simulations showed suppression of coherent false targets with higher peak signal-to-jamming-plus-noise ratios than a reference method across tested SNR and JSR ranges.

papers.title: Perioperative management of patients with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery: A modified Delphi consensus study.
papers.summary: Conducted a two-round modified Delphi study with 35 international experts to generate consensus on perioperative management of adults with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery. Consensus supported preoperative screening, avoidance of hypoxia/hypocapnia/hypotension, deferring elective surgery until symptom resolution, counseling, and structured follow-up, while anesthetic technique, EEG depth monitoring, and neuraxial opioid use remained unresolved.

papers.title: Balanced Block of hERG/Kv11.1, CaV1.2, and NaV1.5 in Proarrhythmic Risk Assessment: An Integrated Review of In Vitro Electrophysiology, In Silico Modeling, and hiPSC-CM Evidence.
papers.summary: Narratively reviewed balanced hERG/Kv11.1, CaV1.2, and NaV1.5 block for proarrhythmic risk assessment, integrating recombinant-cell electrophysiology, in silico modeling, and hiPSC-CM evidence. Concluded that potency ratios alone cannot establish a validated risk threshold, that CiPA-modified O'Hara-Rudy/qNet metrics are model-specific integrators, and that hiPSC-CMs provide complementary but immaturity-limited evidence.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
